label: Broad arrow marks the Board of Ordnance
detail: The three-line broad arrow, later cut under every OS benchmark, had become the mark of the Board of Ordnance.

label: Graff credited with the first post hydrant
detail: Frederick Graff of Philadelphia is traditionally credited with the modern fire hydrant; no patent can be confirmed.

label: Boston Gas Light Co. founded
detail: Earliest ancestor of the gas company whose B.C.G.Co initials are on Boston covers.

label: Patent Office fire
detail: The US Patent Office fire destroys records, which is why Graff's hydrant patent cannot be confirmed.

label: Hyatt patents vault lights
detail: Thaddeus Hyatt patents round glass lenses set in cast-iron sidewalk panels.

label: First street mailboxes
detail: First cast-iron collection boxes mounted on light posts in Boston, Philadelphia and New York.

label: Belgian block in New York
detail: Tooled granite block introduced in New York, general after 1859; rounded cobbles used until about 1860.

label: Boston switches on the first fire alarm telegraph
detail: Channing and Farmer's system opens with 40 boxes and 19 bells; Wikipedia gives April 29, the Boston Globe April 28.

label: Boston fire alarm telegraph switched on
detail: The world's first municipal fire alarm telegraph goes live in Boston.

label: Pont-a-Mousson foundry founded
detail: The French foundry whose name appears on many Paris covers.

label: Fire alarm telegraph patent
detail: Channing and Farmer receive US patent 17,355.

label: Gamewell buys the rights
detail: John N. Gamewell buys the rights to the fire alarm telegraph.

label: Coal-hole plates from 2s 9d
detail: Hayward Brothers advertises 12-inch coal-hole covers in London.

label: Gas-lit signal in Parliament Square
detail: The first traffic signals, gas-lit semaphores, go up in London's Parliament Square.

label: Gamewell company formed
detail: The Gamewell Fire Alarm Telegraph Co. is formed; by 1890 its systems are in 500 cities.

label: Boston underground electric network begins
detail: Eversource's secondary network in Boston dates to the late 1880s.

label: New York steam service begins
detail: Con Edison's predecessor starts district steam in the Financial District in March.

label: Edison Electric Illuminating Co. of Boston founded
detail: Its EEI initials still appear on Boston covers.

label: First listed GPO joint box cover
detail: Joint Box Cover 3 is the earliest in the British telephone cover lists.

label: Gamewell dominates
detail: Gamewell holds 95% of the US fire alarm telegraph market.

label: First painted center line
detail: Edward N. Hines's center line on River Road, Trenton, Wayne County, Michigan.

label: First OS flush brackets
detail: Ordnance Survey flush brackets with plain numbers 1 to 3000 were used from 1912 to 1921.

label: Electric traffic light in Salt Lake City
detail: Lester Wire builds an electric traffic light.

label: Early Detroit stop sign
detail: Wikipedia credits Detroit police sergeant Harry Jackson with a 1914 stop sign; Signalfan dates the first recorded sign to 1915.

label: Electric signal in Cleveland
detail: The American Traffic Signal Co. installs an electric signal in Cleveland, Ohio.

label: McCarroll paints a center stripe
detail: Dr. June McCarroll hand-paints a white stripe near Indio, California, in the fall; Oregon also paints a yellow center line on the Columbia River Highway that year.

label: Nashua's triangular sewer covers
detail: Nashua Foundry begins casting triangular covers at engineer Walter Ellis's suggestion.

label: Beacon Hill Civic Association forms
detail: Residents organize to oppose paving over brick sidewalks.

label: Beacon Hill defends brick
detail: Beacon Hill Civic Association forms to oppose paving over brick sidewalks.

label: Octagon chosen for stop signs
detail: An AASHO-backed committee picks the octagon so the sign is recognizable even from behind.

label: Benchmark C9 set in Yellowstone
detail: The US Coast and Geodetic Survey set disk C9, stamped with an elevation of 7337.580 ft.

label: California adopts center striping
detail: The California Highway Commission adopts striping in November and paints 3,500 miles.

label: Stop signs set to yellow
detail: Yellow is used because no fade-resistant red material exists; it lasts until 1954.

label: Belisha beacons introduced
detail: UK Road Traffic Act 1934 introduces beacons at crossings marked by metal studs.

label: OS G-series flush brackets
detail: Flush brackets with a G prefix first appear.

label: DIN 1451 becomes a German standard
detail: After a 1931 preliminary sheet, DIN 1451 is standardized; a 1938 order requires it on the Autobahn.

label: WPA sidewalk stamps
detail: Dated WPA stamps in Lordsburg NM (1936, 1938), Provo UT (1939) and Knights Landing CA (1940).

label: UK hydrant plates go black on yellow
detail: The wartime National Fire Service adopts black-on-yellow hydrant plates for visibility in all light.

label: Highway Gothic published
detail: The FHWA Standard Alphabets are published; the same year's MUTCD requires reflectorized regulatory and warning signs.

label: Last Watertown-Central Square trolley
detail: The line whose rails were uncovered under Arsenal Street in 2016 ends trolley service.

label: First UK zebra crossing
detail: Striped zebra crossing opens on Slough High Street on 31 October.

label: Freedom Trail dedicated
detail: Mayor John B. Hynes dedicates the trail, marked only by signs at 30 corners.

label: Stop signs turn red
detail: The MUTCD changes stop signs to white on red, matching traffic signals.

label: Interstate shield adopted
detail: AASHO approves the shield, combining Missouri and Texas designs.

label: Freedom Trail red line added
detail: Dick Berenson's idea of a painted red line is carried out.

label: Green chosen for Interstate guide signs
detail: After a Capital Beltway test in which 58 percent picked green, the color is approved in January 1958.

label: Ampelmännchen presented
detail: Karl Peglau presents the East German pedestrian figure.

label: Tenji blocks invented
detail: Seiichi Miyake invents tactile paving in Okayama, Japan, with his own money.

label: UK Worboys sign system becomes law
detail: Kinneir and Calvert's signs and the Transport typeface become the national system.

label: MBTA line colors assigned
detail: Cambridge Seven's color-coded lines are adopted; the T logo appears in the 1965 annual report.

label: T logo codified
detail: The MBTA Manual of Guidelines and Standards fixes the Helvetica T in a black circle.

label: Botts' dots required in California
detail: California requires the ceramic dots in all non-snow areas.

label: First tenji blocks installed
detail: First installation at a school for the blind in Okayama City, by the most cited account; one source says March 1965.

label: Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals
detail: Concluded 8 November 1968; Article 29 allows white or yellow markings, blue for parking.

label: Vienna Convention signed
detail: The UN treaty on road signs is signed; it enters into force on 6 June 1978.

label: Ampelmännchen tested on Unter den Linden
detail: First successful testing of the figure in East Berlin.

label: Yellow center lines mandatory in the US
detail: MUTCD makes yellow the color separating opposing traffic and introduces red markings.

label: Freedom Trail reaches Charlestown
detail: The trail is extended across the river.

label: Japan's bluest green
detail: Japan sets the go light to the bluest possible shade of green.

label: USPS low-volume box guideline
detail: Boxes averaging fewer than 25 pieces a day to be considered for removal.

label: KnoxBox developed
detail: The KnoxBox rapid-entry key box is developed for fire departments.

label: BS 3251 published
detail: The British Standard for hydrant indicator plates, still current, is issued.

label: BWSC created
detail: Boston Water and Sewer Commission takes over from Boston Water Works.

label: Bicycle-safe grate manual
detail: FHWA picks three bike-safe grate designs out of 11 tested.

label: Boston plans to remove its fire boxes
detail: With 1,420 street boxes, the city plans removal around 1990; it never happens.

label: London's first red routes
detail: Red routes introduced in north and east London.

label: Save the Ampelmännchen
detail: A committee forms to bring back the East German figure.

label: JIS T 9251
detail: Japan standardizes tactile block patterns after more than 50 variations.

label: Pipeline Safety Improvement Act
detail: The act provided the statutory basis for a national three-digit call-before-you-dig number.

label: FHWA encourages domes
detail: FHWA memo encourages detectable warnings on curb ramps in federally funded projects.

label: Clearview gets interim approval
detail: FHWA issues IA-5 allowing Clearview on light-on-dark guide signs.

label: FCC designates 811
detail: FCC order 05-59 designated 811 for state one-call systems; carriers had two years from Federal Register publication to implement.

label: Evacuation route signs downtown
detail: Signs go up on every major downtown thoroughfare pointing to evacuation routes.

label: 811 launches nationally
detail: CGA, the FCC and Transportation Secretary Mary Peters launched 811 at a press conference.

label: US manhole cover theft wave
detail: Long Beach, Philadelphia and Chicago report thefts as scrap prices rise.

label: Sign retroreflectivity rule takes effect
detail: Agencies must use a method to keep signs above minimum night visibility levels.

label: Sharrow enters the MUTCD
detail: The shared lane marking is added to the US manual.

label: Flashing yellow arrow authorized
detail: The federal MUTCD formally authorizes the flashing yellow arrow for permissive left turns.

label: No net new brick
detail: Boston adopts a no-net-new-brick sidewalk policy and bans City Hall pavers.

label: NFPA 24 relaxes the PIV rule
detail: After 2010, NFPA 24 allows wall indicator valves and other options instead of a PIV on most private fire mains.

label: Hubway launches
detail: Boston's bike share, now Bluebikes, opens with 60 stations and 600 bikes.

label: Boston launches Adopt-A-Hydrant
detail: In January 2011 Boston residents can claim and name a hydrant and promise to shovel it out.

label: Green bike lanes allowed by interim approval
detail: FHWA Interim Approval IA-14 issued April 15, 2011.

label: Hubway launches in Boston
detail: Boston's bike share opens; it is renamed Bluebikes on May 9, 2018.

label: Boston pilots LED street name signs
detail: LED-lit signs about 35 percent larger go up at three Downtown Crossing locations.

label: Beacon Hill rejects ramp plan
detail: Beacon Hill Architectural Commission votes 3-2 against concrete ramps with plastic tactile panels.

label: PAS 128 first published
detail: BSI's specification for underground utility detection, verification and location was first published.

label: HSG47 third edition
detail: HSE published the third edition of Avoiding danger from underground services.

label: First Japanese manhole cards
detail: April: 30 designs from 28 municipalities.

label: Clearview approval terminated
detail: FHWA ends IA-5; Congress forces its reinstatement on March 28, 2018.

label: Caltrans phases out Botts' dots
detail: Caltrans announces on May 24, 2017 that dots will be replaced with thermoplastic striping.

label: NESC streetlight clearance raised
detail: The NESC raises clearance for ungrounded streetlights from 20 to 40 inches.

label: Japan adds English to stop signs
detail: Bilingual stop and slow signs roll out from July 2017 ahead of the Tokyo Olympics.

label: Fire box beats a 911 outage
detail: On December 28, 2018, a North End fire is reported from a street box during a 911 outage.

label: FCC small cell ruling
detail: US cities may not prohibit small cells in the right-of-way but may set design guidelines.

label: Red transit lanes allowed by interim approval
detail: FHWA Interim Approval IA-22 issued December 4, 2019.

label: USPS pauses box removals
detail: Removals paused until after the November election following social media criticism.

label: New Hampshire's first blue enforcement light
detail: Hudson, NH installs a light that shows blue when the signal is red.

label: UK tactile guidance
detail: DfT publishes new tactile paving guidance replacing the 1998 version.

label: City plans gas lamp replacement
detail: Boston says it plans to replace all its gas lamps with LEDs.

label: Revised PAS 128
detail: ICE and BSI launched a revised PAS 128 with practitioner training and detection accuracy guidance.

label: Manhole cards pass 10 million
detail: July: 968 designs from 668 municipalities and bodies, about 10.5 million cards.

label: MUTCD 11th edition
detail: Published December 2023, incorporating green bike pavement, bike boxes, two-stage turn boxes and red transit lanes in whole or in part.

label: Geocaching retires benchmarking
detail: Geocaching.com stopped hosting its benchmark-hunting section; retirement notes are dated October 17, 2022.

label: PROWAG final rule
detail: Access Board publishes PROWAG, effective September 7, 2023.

label: Statewide 911 outage
detail: During the June 2024 Massachusetts 911 outage, officials urge residents to use fire alarm boxes.

label: 196,977 utility damages
detail: CGA's DIRT report counted 196,977 damages; failure to notify 811 was the top root cause at 24.54 percent.

label: Fire boxes work through 911 outage
detail: Boston's street boxes keep working during the statewide 911 outage.

label: Bluebikes expansion in Boston
detail: Boston begins a 100-station expansion with new solar Pillar docks.

label: California limits sharrows
detail: No new sharrows on roads posted above 30 mph from January 1, 2025, under SB 1216.
